newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, spreads mostly wider.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, spreads mostly wider.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rode higher on the coattails of a Treasury market rally on Wednesday, traders said.
In late trading, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 4/32 at 99-15/32, yielding 96 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 7/32 at 99-17/32, and Freddie Macs were up 8/32 at 99-24/32.
The 10-year note was up 10/32 at 6.67 percent.
An unexpected decline in the Producer Price Index (PPI) set a positive tone for the U.S. credit markets, analysts said.

PPI fell 0.6 percent overall and dipped 0.1 percent excluding volatile food and energy prices. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected headline PPI would be unchanged, with the core index up 0.1 percent.

"We've yet to see any price pressures on the wholesale level," said Kevin Flanagan, vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds. "It will have to enter into discussions at the Fed."
